title: Best Dehumidifier for a Pole Barn (2026): Shop & Storage
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for Pole Barns and Workshop Bays
dek: Metal siding, leaky doors and a gravel floor make a pole barn tough to dry. Here's what works, depending on how sealed yours really is.
description: The best dehumidifier for a pole barn in 2026: picks for insulated, powered shop bays, cold unheated barns and older barns with no outlet at all.
intro: Finding the **best dehumidifier for a pole barn** starts with an honest look at the building. Most pole barns are metal siding fastened to a post frame, with a sliding or overhead door that rarely seals, vents at the eaves or ridge, and often a gravel or dirt floor. Every one of those lets humid outdoor air drift in to replace whatever a dehumidifier just removed.

That doesn't mean a dehumidifier can't help — it means the right one depends on how enclosed your space is. An insulated workshop bay with a slab and a tight door behaves like a big garage. An open hay barn behaves like the outdoors. Below are our picks for each situation, from a powered, insulated shop to an old barn that was never wired, plus how to keep tools, tractors and stored feed from paying the price.
topPicksLead: For an insulated, powered pole barn bay, the **Waykar 80-Pint** is the best place to start: plenty of capacity, auto-defrost for cool months and a washable filter that copes with barn dust.

products.name: Waykar 80-Pint Dehumidifier
pros: Big capacity for a large workshop bay
Auto-defrost for cooler spring and fall days
Washable filter handles dust and chaff
cons: Can't overcome open vents or an unsealed door
products.whyWeLoveIt: If your pole barn has a slab floor, a reasonably tight door and power, this is the right first purchase. It has the muscle to dry a large shop space, and its washable filter is a practical advantage in a building that generates far more dust than a basement.
products.performance: It's an 80-pint-class compressor dehumidifier with auto-defrost, which keeps it working into the cooler shoulder months, down to roughly the low 40s. Hook up a hose and it will drain continuously so you don't have to empty a bucket on every visit. In a barn with open eaves or a door that never closes fully, though, it will run nonstop without getting far — fix the gaps first. See more of the brand in our [Waykar dehumidifier guide](/best/best-waykar-dehumidifier/).

products.name: AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S Dehumidifier
pros: Auto-defrost keeps it working to about 36°F
Built-in pump moves water to a distant drain
cons: Significantly more expensive than a home unit
Still needs a reasonably enclosed space
products.whyWeLoveIt: A bigger or colder pole barn needs something tougher than a household appliance. The HDi65S is built for crawl spaces and basements that run cold and damp year-round, and its pump means you don't have to place it near the one drain in a large building.
products.performance: AlorAir lists defrost operation down to about 36°F, well below where standard compressor units stall. The pump pushes water up and out through a hose, so you can send it out a wall or to a distant drain. It's built to run for years in tough conditions rather than a few summers in a finished basement. If your barn is closer to an open commercial floor, see our [warehouse dehumidifier guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-warehouse/).

products.name: AlorAir Sentinel HDi90 Dehumidifier
pros: 90 pints a day (AHAM) for spaces up to about 2,600 sq ft
cons: Wasted on a barn with open sides or vents
Gravity drain unless you add AlorAir’s optional pump
Louder than Aprilaire and Santa Fe, per owners
products.whyWeLoveIt: When a big pole barn is genuinely built out — insulated walls, a sealed door, no open venting — the HDi90 gives you more capacity than the HDi65S without jumping to industrial equipment. It’s a good match for a large equipment bay or a full-size workshop, and its duct collar lets one unit reach a partitioned space.
products.performance: AlorAir rates it at 90 pints a day under AHAM conditions (198 at saturation) for roughly 2,600 square feet, with defrost operation down to about 33.8°F. It only delivers that coverage in a space that actually holds its air, so seal the structure first. It drains by gravity hose, so plan a route to a floor drain or add the optional pump. More of the range is in our [best AlorAir dehumidifier](/best/best-alorair-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.award: Best value for a single bay
pros: Right-sized for one enclosed room or bay
Widely available and ENERGY STAR certified

products.whyWeLoveIt: Not every pole barn needs commercial hardware. If you only need to protect a closed-off tack room, workshop corner or feed room, this dependable 50-pint unit does the job for far less than the AlorAir models.
products.performance: It's rated at 50 pints a day under the DOE 2019 test, with auto-defrost, a hose connection and auto-restart after a power blip — useful in an outbuilding you don't check every day. It's the same unit we recommend for [garages](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-garage/) and cabins, and it's at its best in a space that stays above the low 40s.

products.name: DampRid Hanging Moisture Absorber
cons: Disposable — replace every month or two
products.whyWeLoveIt: Plenty of older agricultural pole barns were never wired. An electric dehumidifier isn't an option there at any price, but a few DampRid bags around a tack room, feed area or tool cabinet give real, localized protection against rust and mildew.
products.performance: Each bag holds calcium chloride crystals that pull moisture from the air and collect it as liquid. They won't dry an open barn, but in a closed cabinet or small room they help. Expect to replace them every 30 to 60 days depending on conditions. For renewable options, see our [moisture absorber guide](/best/best-moisture-absorber/).

sections.heading: How we pick pole barn dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. We compared rated capacities, coverage claims, low-temperature defrost ratings and drainage designs from manufacturer spec sheets and manuals, then read owner reviews from people using these units in barns, shops and outbuildings — paying special attention to reports about dust-clogged filters, pump failures and frosting in cold weather.
Because pole barns vary so much, we ranked by situation: insulated and powered, large or cold, single enclosed bay, and no power at all.

sections.heading: What to look for in a dehumidifier for a pole barn

items.label: How sealed is the building?
items.text: Gaps around doors, open eave or ridge vents and a dirt floor let wet air pour in. Seal what you can before you size a machine.

items.label: Low-temperature defrost
items.text: If the barn goes unheated, choose a unit rated to defrost into the 30s, or consider a [desiccant dehumidifier](/best/best-desiccant-dehumidifier/).

items.label: A pump or long drain run
items.text: Big buildings rarely have a drain where you need one. A built-in pump gives you flexibility in placement.

items.label: A washable, accessible filter
items.text: Barns are dusty. Plan to clean the filter more often than you would indoors.

items.label: Power — or not
items.text: No wiring means no electric dehumidifier. Use absorbers in closed spaces instead.

sections.heading: Will a dehumidifier work in a pole barn?

blocks.text: Yes, but only in a space that holds its air reasonably well. If you can't seal the whole barn, close off part of it and dry that instead. A walled-in workshop bay or tack room will reach a far lower humidity than an entire open structure ever will.

items: **Weatherstrip the doors.** Add brush or rubber seals to sliding and overhead doors.
**Deal with the floor.** A vapor barrier under gravel, or a poured slab, cuts the moisture rising from the ground.
**Address roof condensation.** Bare metal roofing drips when warm, moist air hits it on cold nights. Insulation or an anti-condensation membrane on the underside helps more than any dehumidifier.
**Close vents only if the barn is otherwise sealed** and not housing animals or curing hay, which need ventilation.
**Then size the dehumidifier** to the enclosed area. Our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) gives a starting point.

blocks.title: Livestock and hay
blocks.text: Barns that house animals or store curing hay need airflow for safety. In those spaces, ventilation — not dehumidification — is the right tool, and a dehumidifier belongs only in a separate, closed-off room.

For an insulated, powered bay, the **Waykar 80-Pint** is the best dehumidifier for a pole barn. Step up to the **AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S** for a cold barn or the **AlorAir HDi90** for a big, fully enclosed one, choose the **Frigidaire FHDD5034W1** for a single room, and use **DampRid** bags if there's no power. Above all, seal the obvious gaps first — a dehumidifier controls humidity, not an open building. For smaller outbuildings, see our [shed picks](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-shed/).

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for a pole barn?
faqs.a: For an insulated, powered bay, the Waykar 80-Pint. For a large or cold barn, the AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S, which defrosts down to about 36°F and has a built-in pump. If the barn has no outlet, DampRid hanging bags are the realistic option.

faqs.q: Will a dehumidifier actually work in a pole barn?
faqs.a: Only if the space holds its air. Gaps around doors, open eave vents and a dirt floor let outside humidity replace what the machine removes. It works well in a sealed barn or in a closed-off room inside a larger one.

faqs.q: Do I need to seal my pole barn before adding a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: You should close the obvious gaps: weatherstrip doors and address the floor and roof condensation. If the barn can't be sealed, dehumidify a smaller enclosed room within it instead.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for a pole barn?
faqs.a: It depends on how enclosed the space is. An insulated bay is well served by an 80-pint unit, while a large sealed barn benefits from a commercial model like the AlorAir HDi90, rated for about 2,600 square feet.

faqs.q: How do I stop condensation on a pole barn's metal roof?
faqs.a: Condensation forms when warm, humid air meets cold roofing. Insulation or an anti-condensation membrane on the underside, plus lower indoor humidity and less ground moisture, are the main fixes.

faqs.q: Will a pole barn dehumidifier work in winter?
faqs.a: Standard compressor units ice up below about 41°F. The AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S defrosts down to about 36°F, and no-power absorbers like DampRid work at any temperature.
